systemic_changes.what: tools/validate_skills.py warns when a cap ideal skill (no -implement or -use suffix) has neither an adapters[] pair nor an open question naming where its pair lives. C3-001 was a rule that existed only in the author brief's per-layer expectations and in what three of four siblings happened to do; it is now checked. cap-errors, cap-identity and cap-idempotency all pass it - the first two through their existing 'Where does the adapter pair for this capability live' open questions, the third through the pair added above.

tools/validate_skills.py's compose-by-name check could not be satisfied by an adapter row: it looked for the owning skill's name only in text/action/why/note, and an adapter row's prose lives in maps_to, cannot and swap_procedure, so such a row warned however it was written. It now reads those fields, plus an open question's question/evidence/default and an operation's input/output. Warning count fell from 139 to 138 with the same skills on disk, and the two warnings the C3-001 fix would otherwise have introduced are now answerable by naming the owner, which is what the rule asks for.

state/loop-workflow.js no longer hands every section a ceremony number derived from a fixed base. The base seeds the first section only; after each section the loop takes the number the improver reports as numbers.ceremony and counts on from there, logging when it differs from what it asked for. The improver prompt now asks for that number. Three sections running were handed a stale number and had to renumber themselves under 1-3-1; a runner that cannot learn from the correction reproduces the collision every section.

build-ceremony instructions step 3 now says to report the number you actually used back to whoever asked for a different one, so its counter self-corrects, with the three consecutive stale numbers as the reason in the why.

lessons_for_next_section: A cap ideal skill states its adapter pair itself: the reader who loads only the ideal facet must be able to name both adapters and the axis their execution models differ on, or swappability is not visibly a tested property of that capability.

When a rule holds in three of four sibling skills, it is a convention that has not been checked. Move it into tools/validate_skills.py in the same ceremony that finds it, so the fourth case is caught at write time rather than at review time.
Moving a fact up from an -implement facet to its ideal facet turns the implement row into a restatement: fix both ends in one edit, naming the new owner in the row you left behind.

A checker that cannot be satisfied by a well-written row is a defect in the checker. The compose-by-name warning looked for the owner's name in fields adapter rows do not have; extending the fields it reads was the fix, not silencing the warning.

The same ceremony-numbering collision three sections running is not three authoring mistakes; it is a runner that derives the number from its own position and never learns the correction. Fix the producer: report the corrected number back and count on from it.
A finding can be right about the habit and wrong about the file. Check the working tree and the reviewed commit before editing, and record 'already correct, verified' rather than a phantom fix.
